verdict.rationale: Vercel documents deploys from standard GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket pushes and supports Next.js plus 40+ other frameworks. Its CLI can be driven by an automated system such as an existing CI pipeline and is Apache-2.0 licensed, and Dockerfile-based apps and the open Build Output API spec reduce reliance on proprietary build tooling. The editor workflow is evidenced only indirectly, through plugins for AI coding tools such as Cursor and GitHub Copilot, and no doc explicitly covers running existing third-party CI pipelines. missing for 10: explicit documentation of existing CI integration (e.g., GitHub Actions/GitLab CI recipes), evidence that editor workflows need no Vercel-specific tooling, independent or hands-on corroboration of lock-in-free workflows.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Connect GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket to deploy on every push, with a preview URL for every branch.
Deploy Next.js with zero configuration, or bring one of 40+ supported frameworks.
With the command-line interface (CLI) you can interact with the Vercel platform using a terminal, or through an automated system
Run any code and library on Vercel Functions with an OCI container image built from a Dockerfile or Containerfile at the project root.
